title: The invisible forest of the sea
text: The name plankton comes {{1}} the Greek for 'wanderer', {{2}} suits organisms that drift {{3}} the mercy of the currents. {{4}} of them are microscopic plants, collectively called phytoplankton, which capture sunlight just {{5}} plants on land do. Together they account {{6}} roughly half of the oxygen in every breath you take, and they underpin the entire marine food web, feeding everything from krill to blue whales. Yet remarkably {{7}} of us ever give them a thought. Warmer seas and acidifying water {{8}} already shifting plankton populations, with consequences that could reach every dinner table on the planet.

gaps.explanation: 'Come from' — from introduces the source of the name.
Non-defining relative referring back to the whole fact about the name.

gaps.hint: preposition: ___ the mercy of the currents
gaps.explanation: 'At the mercy of' is the fixed phrase meaning 'entirely controlled by'.
'Most of them' — the majority of the two great plankton groups are plants.

gaps.hint: conjunction: just ___ plants on land do
gaps.explanation: 'Just as … do' — the comparative conjunction of manner.

gaps.hint: preposition: account ___ half of the oxygen
gaps.explanation: 'Account for' — the fixed verb phrase meaning 'make up'.
'Few of us' with the plural verb 'give'; 'little' cannot stand before 'of us'.

gaps.hint: verb: water and acid ___ already shifting
gaps.explanation: Present continuous with a plural subject: seas and water are shifting.
